title: When Speculation Spills Secrets: Side Channels via Speculative Decoding In LLMs
quote: leak confidential datastore contents used for prediction at rates exceeding 25 tokens/sec
proves: Per-iteration token counts or packet sizes reveal input-dependent accept/reject patterns; fingerprinting over 50 prompts >75% accurate across REST, LADE, BiLD, EAGLE; still far above 2% chance at T=1.0; datastore leak >25 tok/s; mitigations = packet padding and iteration-wise token aggregation
does_not_prove: Threat model is network observer or malicious user against a single deployment; no co-tenant attacker, no batching or multi-tenant analysis; no throughput cost of mitigations
bearing: Supports isolation candidates that treat accepted length as a leaked signal; threatens any claim that SD side channels are unstudied

title: When Speculation Spills Secrets (v4 HTML: mitigations, threat model, datastore)
quote: ensure any data-store used for speculation (like in REST) only contains public data
proves: Constant 1024-byte padding cuts accuracy to chance but inflates payload 230x; aggregation over 20 iterations leaves 9.2%/52%/11.2% accuracy for LADE/REST/BiLD; datastore attack shown only on REST with a fixed ShareGPT datastore; paper says user-derived datastores may be leaked but does not test it; SuffixDecoding and cross-user leakage not mentioned
does_not_prove: Never tests a runtime cache populated by OTHER users' outputs (suffix global tree, SGLang NGRAM trie, llama.cpp ngram-mod); no co-tenant model; no engine-level defense like per-tenant cache keys
bearing: Leaves open cross-tenant leakage via shared online draft caches

title: Remote Timing Attacks on Efficient Language Model Inference
quote: But these techniques introduce data-dependent timing characteristics.
proves: Efficiency techniques such as speculative sampling make timing data-dependent; topic of a conversation learnable with 90%+ precision on open-source systems from encrypted traffic
does_not_prove: General efficiency-timing attack; not specific to batch co-tenancy or shared draft caches
bearing: Prior art for SD timing leakage; threatens novelty of a pure network-timing attack

title: Whisper Leak: a side-channel attack on Large Language Models
quote: none provides complete protection
proves: Packet size and timing of streamed responses classify prompt topics across 28 LLMs, often >98% AUPRC; random padding, token batching, packet injection all incomplete
does_not_prove: Abstract does not mention speculative decoding; does not separate SD-induced bursts from ordinary streaming
bearing: Shows streaming-level defenses are incomplete; SD-specific defenses still open

title: Adversarial Prompts for Acceptance Collapse in Speculative Decoding
quote: batched serving couples requests through shared GPU execution
proves: Adversarial suffix collapses acceptance; +62.3% mean sample time on GSM8K with task quality kept; tested tokenwise, blockwise, HSD, EAGLE-3 and independent drafts; proposed defense is monitoring acceptance and disabling speculation or routing to target-only
does_not_prove: Impact on co-scheduled benign users is argued, not measured; no vLLM/SGLang batch experiment; n-gram drafting not tested
bearing: Strongly supports a gap: measured cross-request harm of a low-acceptance (or adversarial) request inside a shared batch

title: vLLM design doc: Automatic Prefix Caching (Cache Isolation for Security)
quote: ensuring that only requests with the same salt can reuse cached KV blocks.
proves: Prefix cache has per-request cache_salt so reuse is limited to a trust group, explicitly to block timing attacks
does_not_prove: Covers KV prefix cache only; nothing about speculative draft caches
bearing: Baseline isolation mechanism that draft caches lack (see F7-F12)

title: vLLM SuffixDecodingProposer source (vllm/v1/spec_decode/suffix_decoding.py)
quote: self.suffix_cache.start_request(req_id, prompt_token_ids)
proves: Only req_id and tokens are passed to the shared SuffixDecodingCache; no tenant, LoRA id, or cache_salt reaches it
does_not_prove: Internal keying of Arctic SuffixDecodingCache not shown on this page
bearing: Supports gap: global suffix tree has no trust-group scoping in vLLM

title: vLLM SpeculativeConfig API reference (suffix_decoding_max_cached_requests)
quote: If set to 0, the global suffix tree is disabled and past responses are not cached (prompt trees are still used).
proves: Only isolation knob is all-or-nothing: disable the global tree for everyone; no LoRA field and no per-request speculation disable in SpeculativeConfig
does_not_prove: Does not quantify how much acceptance is lost by disabling the global tree
bearing: Supports per-tenant (salted) global suffix tree as a candidate; cost of all-or-nothing switch unmeasured

title: Arctic Inference: Suffix Decoding docs
quote: Contains historical outputs from completed requests, capturing common patterns across requests.
proves: Global tree stores outputs of completed requests across requests; suffix_cache_max_requests default 100000 with FIFO eviction; no per-user isolation or privacy note
does_not_prove: No measurement of how much speedup comes from cross-request (vs same-tenant) matches
bearing: Shared cross-request state = cross-tenant leakage surface; also performance-isolation question (tenant A's outputs evicting B's)

title: SGLang ngram_worker.py source (_update_ngram_corpus)
quote: self.ngram_corpus.batch_put(batch_tokens)
proves: One NgramCorpus per worker; every request in the batch inserts its prompt tail and output tokens into the same online trie; no tenant, LoRA, or salt key on insert
does_not_prove: Does not show whether matches actually cross tenants often enough to matter or be exploitable
bearing: Supports cross-tenant leakage gap in SGLang NGRAM drafting

title: SGLang docs: Speculative Decoding (NGRAM)
quote: Cache capacity (number of entries).
proves: NGRAM drafts from a cache built from previously generated tokens; --speculative-ngram-capacity default 10,000,000; only server-level flags, no per-request controls, no LoRA note
does_not_prove: Docs do not state sharing scope (source F10 does)
bearing: Supports gap: no documented isolation for n-gram draft cache

title: llama.cpp docs/speculative.md
quote: Currently, a single hash pool is shared across all server slots, so different requests can benefit from each other.
proves: llama-server ngram-mod uses one hash pool shared by all slots; no isolation note
does_not_prove: No security analysis or measurement of cross-slot benefit
bearing: Third engine with a shared cross-request draft cache; relevant to Mac-local experiments

title: Governing the KV Cache: Preventing Timing Side-Channel Leakage in Multi-Tenant LLM Inference
quote: reconstruct another tenant's private prompt by probing cache-hit latency
proves: Per-principal salted block hashes make KV cache keys disjoint across tenants; salting at divergence point keeps ~93% of prefix-cache benefit; cold/cached TTFT ratio 0.22 on vLLM A100
does_not_prove: Prefix cache only; no mention of speculative, n-gram, or draft caches; defense evaluated in simulation
bearing: Template for a per-tenant draft-cache defense and its benefit-retention metric; shows the analogous draft-cache problem is unaddressed

title: [Feature]: Ensure output consistency when using LoRA with Eagle3 Speculative Decoding (vLLM #26679)
quote: The problem I'm observing is not a crash, but incorrect output.
proves: LoRA + EAGLE-3 output differed from LoRA-only output; later attributed to batching numerics; closed not-planned Feb 2026 for inactivity
does_not_prove: No resolution on whether the drafter sees the adapter
bearing: Shows LoRA+SD correctness was uncertain into 2026

title: [Bugfix][LoRA][Spec Decode] Support LoRA with speculative decoding (vLLM PR #21068)
quote: it assumes 1 sampled token for each prompt in each forward pass step
proves: V1 LoRA mapped one adapter id per request; with SD the logits have K+1 rows per request; fix stores LoRA id per sampled token
does_not_prove: Target-side only; no drafter adaptation; no acceptance or throughput data
bearing: Establishes vLLM LoRA+SD = shared unadapted drafter

title: [Bug]: Model Runner V2 maps lm_head LoRA per request instead of per logits row under speculative decoding (vLLM #59161)
quote: in a mixed batch its delta can land on a *different* request's logits.
proves: In MRV2 (v0.30.0) with MTP, an lm_head adapter has no effect on its own request and its delta can be applied to a neighbouring request; nothing is logged; fix repeats mapping by logits rows
does_not_prove: Single bug report with local patch; not merged at fetch
bearing: Concrete cross-tenant correctness-isolation failure caused by SD's per-request row expansion

title: Support spec decoding when LoRA is applied to target model (SGLang PR #12903)
quote: as we assume seqlen = 1 during decoding in many places
proves: SGLang LoRA+SD broke because decode assumed seq_len 1; fix generalizes using spec_info.num_tokens_per_bs; tested with NGRAM
does_not_prove: No acceptance or throughput data
bearing: Engine support timeline

title: [Spec][LoRA] Support multi-adapter LoRA with EAGLE/NEXTN/DFLASH/DSPARK speculative decoding (SGLang PR #34337)
quote: Adapters apply to the target model only; one shared draft runs unadapted.
proves: Shared unadapted drafter: public adapters barely move accept length, but heavy-shift adapters cut accept length 19-31% (NEXTN), ~34% (DFLASH), ~41% (EAGLE3); first-token accept for EAGLE3 falls 0.611 to ~0.22; LoRA+spec is 2.12x at c=1 but below no-spec by c=32 (1419.7 vs 2975.4 tok/s); rejects --speculative-adaptive with LoRA
does_not_prove: Accept-length loss measured per adapter in isolation; no per-adapter drafter comparison; no study of mixed-adapter batch effects on SD policy
bearing: Strong support for per-adapter or adapter-aware drafter candidates; shows low-accept adapters co-batched with others

title: [RFC]: LoRA adapter support for DFlash speculative decoding draft models (vLLM #52038)
quote: an R64 adapter is ~28x smaller than the 0.8B drafter it replaces
proves: Proposes drafter-side LoRA routed per request; claims drafter quality within ~2% of a fully trained per-domain drafter (acceptance length); prior V0 attempt hit vocab padding mismatch
does_not_prove: Results withheld (proprietary); no mixed-adapter batching data; not implemented at fetch
bearing: Directly overlaps per-tenant drafter-adapter candidates; implementation still open

title: [Feature] LoRA adapter support for Dspark speculative decoding draft models (SGLang #37772)
quote: so we can choose different draft model to different tasks for higher accept rate
proves: Request for per-task drafter adapters, or multiple drafters for one target, in SGLang
does_not_prove: No design, data, or comments
bearing: Demand signal for drafter multiplexing; open in both engines

title: [Feature][Spec Decode] Add Uno shared-model drafting with a draft-only LoRA adapter (vLLM PR #55947)
quote: refuses a request-specific LoRA adapter with Uno
proves: Target drafts itself through a draft-only LoRA; 2.1-2.4x single stream on GB10, 1.1-1.6x at 4-16 streams; request-specific LoRA adapters are refused
does_not_prove: Cannot coexist with tenant LoRA adapters; no multi-adapter story
bearing: Shows LoRA slot now competes between drafting and tenancy; opening for designs that combine both

title: TensorRT-LLM Feature Combination Matrix
quote: Untested
proves: LoRA row is Untested for all three speculative decoding columns (Linear, Dynamic Trees, Legacy NGram)
does_not_prove: Untested is not unsupported; no data
bearing: TRT-LLM has no validated LoRA+SD path

title: Fireworks docs: Understanding LoRA performance
quote: trained LoRA deployments may not unless you configure a custom draft model.
proves: Production provider: LoRA deployments often lack SD; a custom draft per trained model can match base latency; multi-LoRA TTFT often +10-30% vs live merge
does_not_prove: No numbers on acceptance with shared vs custom drafts; enterprise feature, no design detail
bearing: Workload evidence that per-fine-tune drafters are the practical answer today

title: [Feature] Per-request opt-out of speculative decoding (SGLang RFC #30263)
quote: Batch-granular: mixed batches still speculate for everyone.
proves: SD is all-or-nothing per server; per-request opt-out needs a CUDA-graph runtime-state swap because verify assumes num_tokens_per_req == draft_token_num; option B (homogeneous-batch scheduling) left as future; notes opted-out batches would drag the shared adaptive EMA; vLLM #7569 and #17984 closed not-planned
does_not_prove: Design only; no measurements; closed by stale bot
bearing: Supports performance-isolation gap: one request class cannot escape the batch's speculation width, and shared adaptive state couples tenants

title: [Feature]: Restore length-based speculation skip or per-request speculative decoding control in V1 (vLLM #52258)
quote: collapses to 5–8% acceptance, making speculation net-negative
proves: On one engine, long-document requests reach 5-8% acceptance while short ones get 1.6-1.8x; V1 has no per-request skip; SpeculativeConfig.max_model_len is a no-op
does_not_prove: User report; does not measure effect of the low-accept requests on co-batched short ones
bearing: Real mixed-workload evidence for per-request/per-class speculation control

title: [RFC]: Per-request effective proposal lengths for adaptive speculative decoding (vLLM #48202)
quote: A uniform K, however well chosen, pays for this within-batch spread
proves: Within one MT-Bench batch, DSpark confident-prefix lengths span 0..7 (e.g. [7,4,0,7,2,1,0,0]); vLLM draft outputs are fixed-width [batch_size, K] with zero padding; per-request truncation does not change verification on the async path
does_not_prove: Throughput gain of per-request lengths not reported in fetched part
bearing: Quantifies verification padding inside shared batches; per-request length itself is R04-covered adaptive territory

title: vLLM docs: Adaptive Verification
quote: the highest-scoring slots are admitted until a global budget is spent.
proves: Draft slots from all requests compete for one global verify budget ranked by survival probability
does_not_prove: No per-request floor, priority, or fairness guarantee described
bearing: Opening: fairness/priority-aware verify budget across tenants (confident requests can starve others' slots)

title: FASER: Fine-Grained Phase Management for Speculative Decoding in Dynamic LLM Serving
quote: dynamically adjusting the speculative length for each request within a continuous batch
proves: Per-request speculative length plus early pruning of rejected tokens in vLLM; up to 53% throughput and 1.92x lower latency
does_not_prove: Optimizes aggregate throughput/latency; no tenant fairness or isolation metric in abstract
bearing: Threatens per-request-length candidates; leaves fairness framing open

title: AdaServe: Accelerating Multi-SLO LLM Serving with SLO-Customized Speculative Decoding
quote: constructs a speculation tree tailored to each request's latency target
proves: Per-request speculation trees by SLO; up to 4.3x fewer SLO violations, 1.9x goodput
does_not_prove: Priority classes via latency targets only; no adversarial or low-accept tenant, no multi-LoRA
bearing: Largely answers QoS/priority-class speculation

title: TETRIS: Optimal Draft Token Selection for Batch Speculative Decoding
quote: TETRIS actively selects the most promising draft tokens (for every request in a batch)
proves: Batch-level draft token selection across requests to maximize total throughput
does_not_prove: Aggregate objective; no per-request fairness or tenant guarantee
bearing: Same as F27: throughput-optimal cross-request allocation without fairness

title: DSpark: Confidence-Scheduled Speculative Decoding with Semi-Autoregressive Generation
quote: wastes critical batch capacity on tokens with high rejection risks
proves: Verifying long low-confidence blocks wastes batch capacity under high concurrency; per-request confidence-scheduled verification gives 60-85% faster per-user speed at matched throughput in DeepSeek-V4 serving
does_not_prove: No per-tenant breakdown; capacity waste not quantified in abstract
bearing: Confirms cross-request capacity coupling is real in production

title: [RFC]: Disaggregated Speculative Decoding with Standalone Parallel Draft Model (vLLM #42109)

does_not_prove: POC numbers without methodology; isolation is per verify server, not per tenant; no fairness across targets
bearing: Directly overlaps 'many targets share one drafter' candidates
